verdicts.reason: No Los Angeles document addresses application or screening fees. The retrieved passages (D026, DX08) describe a $30 CPI-adjusted screening fee cap that appears to be California state law (Berkeley's D005 cites Civil Code 1950.6), which would apply in LA. That suggests a rule may exist, and nothing shows LA has none.

No Los Angeles document addresses tenant screening criteria. The retrieved passages describe California regulations limiting criminal-history screening (DX07) and source-of-income and credit-history provisions (D027) that may apply statewide. Nothing establishes that LA lacks such restrictions.

D039 is a 2024 council motion asking LAHD to report on the feasibility of banning algorithmic rent-setting software. It shows no ban existed when the motion was filed but does not show whether one was later adopted. DX09 also describes a California prohibition on common pricing algorithms that may apply in LA. The status is not settled.
